newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine stocks surge to record.
newsitem.headline: Philippine stocks surge to record.

text.p: Philippine shares fleetingly surged above an all-time high on Wednesday and analysts said the stock market was gearing to break more records on the back of good company earnings and strong economic performance.

"Success builds on success and once people see a market such as the Philippines trying to break out of its record high, they just want to be in," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor Hagedorn Securities Inc.

In late trade on Wednesday, the market reached a new high of 3,376.51, breaking the 3,375.94 level reached last July. It closed slightly lower at 3,373.61 points, up 31.62 points, or 0.95 percent, from the previous close.

The intra-day record triggered optimism among stock analysts, who said the uptrend seemed well supported as Wednesday's trading volume at 5.5 billion pesos ($209 million) was double the average daily volume.
"I think the momentum will be sustained...and there will be no problems in reaching uncharted territories," Wilfred Son Keng Po, chief operating officer at Angping Securities, said.
Son Keng Po predicted the index would soon reach 3,500 points at least.
Brokerage Anscor Hagedorn said it saw the index at 3,400 in February while Dharmala Securities Phils Inc forecast 3,600 within the second quarter.
"Good earnings and strong economic fundamentals will beef up the market," said Fitz Aclan, research head at Dharmala Securities.

Analysts' expectations of a rosy economic picture were confirmed after the market closed when the government announced that gross national product (GNP) had grown by 6.8 percent in 1996, up from 5.0 percent in 1995.
Though the figure was below expectations of some government officials, analysts said they were pleased with the numbers.
"It's within expectation and the market will likely react positively," Aclan said.

Announcing the GNP figures, Socio-Economic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito said the government expected a 7.0 to 8.0 percent GNP growth in 1997. He said inflation would slow down further to 6-6.5 percent from 8.4 percent last year.
Analysts said good corporate results were also boosting the market.
On Wednesday, blue chip San Miguel Corp reported a marginal rise in 1996 net income to 6.09 billion pesos ($232 million) from 5.84 billion ($222 million) in the previous year.
The 1996 figure was bolstered by extraordinary gains but analysts said it was much better than expected.
"The net income was slightly positive and not as bad as envisioned by most brokerage houses," said Son Keng Po.
Most other blue chips are yet to announce their results and expectations are that the figures will show robust growth.

"On the whole, a lot of investors are bullish about prospects on the corporate earnings side and one nice thing about the way the index has moved is that unlike the Dow, it's a gradual ascent for our market," Francisco Trinidad, research head at DBS Securities, said.
